text: The induction principle for the identity type — the J rule — has this feature that distinguishes it from K:
choices: J handles arbitrary paths p:a=b (not just loops), K only handles p:a=a
explanation: J (path induction) works for any path p:a=b between potentially different points. K (Streicher's K) specialises to loops p:a=a and adds UIP. K is not derivable from J.
